$$\begin{align*}
\cos 5x + \sin x &= 0 \\
\cos 5x &= -\sin x \\
\cos 5x &= \cos\left(x + \frac{\pi}{2}\right) \\
\end{align*}$$
This yields two sets of general solutions:
Case 1:
$$\begin{align*}
5x &= 2k\pi + x + \frac{\pi}{2} \\
4x &= 2k\pi + \frac{\pi}{2} \\
x &= \frac{k\pi}{2} + \frac{\pi}{8}
\end{align*}$$
For $0 \leq x \leq 2\pi$:
$k=0 \implies x = \frac{\pi}{8}$
$k=1 \implies x = \frac{5\pi}{8}$
$k=2 \implies x = \frac{9\pi}{8}$
$k=3 \implies x = \frac{13\pi}{8}$
(4 solutions)
Case 2:
$$\begin{align*}
5x &= 2k\pi - \left(x + \frac{\pi}{2}\right) \\
6x &= 2k\pi - \frac{\pi}{2} \\
x &= \frac{k\pi}{3} - \frac{\pi}{12}
\end{align*}$$
For $0 \leq x \leq 2\pi$:
$k=1 \implies x = \frac{3\pi}{12} = \frac{\pi}{4}$
$k=2 \implies x = \frac{7\pi}{12}$
$k=3 \implies x = \frac{11\pi}{12}$
$k=4 \implies x = \frac{15\pi}{12} = \frac{5\pi}{4}$
$k=5 \implies x = \frac{19\pi}{12}$
$k=6 \implies x = \frac{23\pi}{12}$
(6 solutions)
Total number of distinct solutions $= 4 + 6 = 10$.
